Hi everyone,

I'm trying to update the DDI codebook metadata xml file of a dataset file using the Dataverse API. The dataset file in question is a .sav file that has been ingested on our Dataverse instance.

I'm using the following curl command:

curl -v \
  -H "X-Dataverse-key:$API_TOKEN" \
  -X PUT \
  "https://dataverse-test.bsc.es/api/edit/3286" \
  --upload-file ddi_corrected.xml

The request completes successfully, returning HTTP 200 OK and the following response:

{"status":"OK","data":{"message":"Nothing to update"}}

See attached .txt file for the full curl output:

dataverse_api_error.txt

The XML file (ddi_corrected.xml) is approximately 608 KB and contains the updated DDI metadata xml.

Does anyone know why Dataverse might return "Nothing to update" despite the PUT request being successful?

Is there a particular API endpoint or XML structure I should be using to update the metadata of an existing Dataset file through the Dataverse API?

Just to give some extra context: the reason why I want to do this is because I noticed that for some categorical variables encoded as numbers in tabular files ingested via Dataverse there are some extra, unnecessary sumStat lines. I thought it would be possible to just update the resulting xml file that has been generated during the ingestion. See below an excerpt from the metadata file in question, with the lines I want to remove commented out:

<var ID="v3242" name="DEVICE" intrvl="discrete">
<location fileid="f3287"/>
<labl level="variable">DEVICE</labl>
<!--
<sumStat type="mode">.</sumStat>
<sumStat type="max">3.0</sumStat>
<sumStat type="min">1.0</sumStat>
<sumStat type="mean">2.44438202247191</sumStat>
<sumStat type="stdev">0.88186201780734</sumStat>
<sumStat type="medn">3.0</sumStat>
<sumStat type="invd">0.0</sumStat>
<sumStat type="vald">1780.0</sumStat>
-->
<catgry>
<catValu>3</catValu>
<labl level="category">Mobile</labl>
<catStat type="freq">1263</catStat>
</catgry>
<catgry>
<catValu>1</catValu>
<labl level="category">Desktop</labl>
<catStat type="freq">472</catStat>
</catgry>
<catgry>
<catValu>2</catValu>
<labl level="category">Tablet</labl>
<catStat type="freq">45</catStat>
</catgry>
<varFormat type="numeric"/>
<notes subject="Universal Numeric Fingerprint" level="variable" type="VDC:UNF">UNF:6:gM8qpKE4+3iy+u9WtjXY8A==</notes>
</var>

Is this a known bug in Dataverse?
Thanks in advance!

Hi. I'm not sure what version you're on, but for the latest, I'm seeing "Nothing to update" in two possible places:

  • https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/v6.12.1/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/EditDDI.java#L151
  • https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/blob/v6.12.1/src/main/java/edu/harvard/iq/dataverse/api/EditDDI.java#L164
@Victoria Lubitch wrote this code and might be able to advise you.

@Paolo Marangio please feel free to go ahead and create a bug.

Also, I'd be interested to know if you can reproduce it on https://demo.dataverse.org

@Philip Durbin 🚀

Just wanted to go over the message I posted at the beginning of this thread and clarify the context for this issue. The reason why I have been trying (unsuccessfully) to manually update the DDI Codebook XML file for my dataset is because Dataverse generates a partially incorrect DDI codebook when it processes categorical variables encoded as numbers. Namely it generates some descriptive statistics, but this does not make sense (i.e. it does not make sense to report the mean of the occurrences of 3 categorical variables encoded as 1, 2 and 3). In the XML file above I sent an excerpt from the .xml file that is generated after pressing on "Access File" --> "DDI Codebook v2" (below "Download Metadata").

Just thought it would be good to highlight this and try to differentiate the two issues here, namely the incorrect lines in the DDI codebook xml file generated for categorical variables and the inability to manually update the DDI codebook of an existing dataset .
"Dataverse generates a partially incorrect DDI codebook when it processes categorical variables encoded as numbers." Interesting. I didn't know this.

Philip Durbin 🚀 said:

"Dataverse generates a partially incorrect DDI codebook when it processes categorical variables encoded as numbers." Interesting. I didn't know this.

Yes. What I meant to say is that Dataverse appears to generate some additional information for categorical variables with numerical values that although could technically be valid according to the DDI Codebook schema, it does not make (statistical) sense. I am saying this based on some answers reported in a conversation I have started in the DDI Google discussion group:

https://groups.google.com/g/icpsr-ddi-users/c/hkAAbmqzH5g/m/r680rkyrBAAJ

Some people hinted to the fact that having sumStat lines in the DDI codebook for a categorical variable with numerical values does not make sense.

From what I understand, the (somewhat unfortunately named :slight_smile:) API above was implemented specifically for the needs of one specific Dataverse instance - Borealis. It only modifies some metadata fields associated with DataVariables in ingested tabular files required by their use case. I don't think it was intended, or guaranteed to cover everything in the variable-level metadata, and/or everything that is included in the DDI produced by Dataverse.
From a quick glance, it does not cover summary statistics at all - so the <sumStat ...> sections in the input are simply ignored. I'm sure it would be possible to extend this, or add another API for editing summary stats as well. Hopefully, Victoria, the author, can give authoritative answers on all this.

As for why these stats were generated in the first place: I know it was a deliberate decision here, at Harvard, a decade or so ago, to calculate these summary stats for all variables that were numeric, including discreet types and/or categorical values. The researchers involved must have had some rationale for this, but it may not be possible to establish what it was at this point. But we should be able to ~ easily make this behavior configurable - i.e., leave it for the admins of specific instances to decide how they want summary stats to be calculated and for what types of variables.

P.S. One potentially easy workaround would be to develop a lightweight export plugin - the format could be named DDI_corrected, for example - dependent on/derivative of our "normal" DDI; that would consume the exported and cached DDI and strip and/or modify some of its sections as needed.
This would be a very similar concept to the already supported "DDI HTML" export plugin; which similarly uses pre-generated DDI and reformats it as html.
